language.scope: Initial target: Python 3.14 language syntax and core semantics as documented by the official Python Language Reference. Use the Python Standard Library reference for built-in functions, built-in constants, built-in types, exceptions, importlib behavior, and modules that materially interact with language semantics. Use accepted/final PEPs as provenance for features, but prefer the current official documentation when it differs from historical PEP text.
non_goals: Python 2 semantics and unsupported Python 3 versions.
Alternate implementation behavior from PyPy, Jython, IronPython, or Python.NET unless a separate profile is explicitly created.
CPython bytecode, compiler optimizations, reference-counting details, C API behavior, ABI behavior, and internal interpreter layout unless they are selected as an implementation profile.
Exhaustive standard-library semantics beyond builtins and modules that affect core language execution.
Third-party packaging, PyPI behavior, virtual environment tooling, and framework/library semantics unless separately chartered.
Host-specific I/O, OS, filesystem, signal, thread scheduling, and locale behavior except through explicit environment profiles.

specifications.title: Python 3.14.6 documentation
specifications.notes: Official documentation for Python 3.14.6; docs.python.org lists Python 3.14 as stable, Python 3.15 as pre-release, and Python 3.16 as in development.

specifications.title: The Python Language Reference
specifications.notes: Primary source for syntax and core semantics. The reference itself states that it is mostly English prose rather than a fully formal specification, so ambiguities must be tracked explicitly.

specifications.title: Python Language Reference: Introduction
specifications.notes: Explains alternate implementations, CPython implementation notes, and the grammar notation used by lexical and syntactic definitions.

specifications.title: Python Language Reference: Full Grammar specification
specifications.notes: Documentation says the full grammar is derived directly from the CPython parser grammar and omits code-generation and error-recovery details.

specifications.title: The Python Standard Library
specifications.notes: Primary source for built-in functions, constants, types, exceptions, importlib, ast, tokenize, token, keyword, and other modules that interact with language execution.

specifications.title: PEP Index
specifications.notes: Use accepted/final Standards Track PEPs to explain feature history and design rationale. Current docs remain canonical for implemented behavior.

reference_implementations.name: CPython 3.14.6
reference_implementations.notes: Use CPython for differential behavior where the language reference is ambiguous or explicitly marks CPython implementation notes. Keep CPython-specific behavior separate from portable Python semantics.

test_suites.name: CPython regression test suite
test_suites.notes: Primary large-scale regression suite for the CPython reference profile. Tests must be classified as language semantics, CPython implementation detail, standard library behavior, platform-dependent behavior, or non-goal.

test_suites.name: Python doctest/unittest examples in official docs
test_suites.role: documentation examples and local golden cases
test_suites.notes: Useful for small golden cases, but examples must be traced to the relevant reference section before they become conformance tests.

known_gaps.description: The Python Language Reference is the official core reference, but it is intentionally written mostly in English rather than as a fully formal semantic specification. Ambiguities must be recorded and tested against CPython where appropriate.

CPython is the primary implementation and practical oracle, but some behavior is documented as implementation-specific. The base semantics must distinguish portable Python behavior from CPython-profile behavior.
The full standard library is enormous. The initial formal semantics should cover builtins and language-interacting modules before attempting broad library semantics.
I/O, filesystem, concurrency, signals, locale, and platform behavior need explicit host profiles to avoid baking in accidental local behavior.
